official.native: Koninkrijk België / Royaume de Belgique / Königreich Belgien

government.note: Federal parliamentary constitutional monarchy. The party system is split by language: almost all parties stand only in Dutch-speaking or only in French-speaking constituencies (PVDA-PTB is an exception), so federal governments are multi-party coalitions across both language groups. Government formation can take very long; the outgoing government stays in office as a caretaker meanwhile (e.g. after the 2010, 2019 and 2024 elections). Since 2014 federal elections are held every five years on the day of the European elections.

system.note: D'Hondt list PR. Since the 2003 electoral code: 11 constituencies (the ten provinces and Brussels) with a 5% threshold per constituency; the threshold was new in 2003. Voting is compulsory. Term four years until 2014, five years since. seats_2000 is the result of the 13 June 1999 election.

source.title: Wikipedia: 2003 Belgian federal election (new electoral code, threshold)

system.note: Until 2014: 40 senators directly elected, 21 community senators and 10 co-opted senators. After the sixth state reform the Senate has not been directly elected; since 2014 it has 60 members (50 from the regional and community parliaments plus 10 co-opted). seats_2000 is the total per party after the 1999 election.
